title: Redefining intranasal brain delivery: from nasal entry to meaningful parenchymal and cellular exposure

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Redefining intranasal brain delivery: from nasal entry to meaningful parenchymal and cellular exposure》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0001-p5】In this context, the present review aims to propose a stage-resolved mechanistic and evaluative framework for N2B delivery (Lochhead and Davis 2019; Wang et al. 2019; Yokel 2022). Specifically, we reconceptualize the N2B pathway as a sequence of transport stages and associated bottlenecks, extending from nasal entry to meaningful parenchymal and cellular access. We further examine the current imbalance in the field, whereby early nasal barriers have been extensively studied, whereas post-entry transport and tissue-access processes remain comparatively under-integrated in both mechanistic discussion and experimental validation (Lochhead and Davis 2019; Wang et al. 2019; Yokel 2022; Drath et al. 2025). On this basis, we systematize the validation criteria required at each stage of delivery and thereby propose an evaluative framework capable of distinguishing meaningful delivery from simple exposure (Lochhead et al. 2015; Ahmad et al. 2017; Yokel 2022). Finally, we discuss how formulation design may need to evolve beyond single-barrier optimization toward multistage-aware, disease-informed, and cargo-informed strategies.

【Introduction · s0001-p1】Recent global burden analyzes indicate that neurological conditions are now the leading cause of illness and disability, affecting more than three billion people globally (Steinmetz et al., 2024). Despite this substantial disease burden, therapeutic progress in central nervous system (CNS) disorders remains limited. A fundamental challenge lies in the difficulty of achieving sufficient and reproducible delivery of therapeutics to diseased brain regions. In particular, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) restricts the entry of over 98% of small-molecule drugs and virtually all macromolecular therapeutics, preventing many promising candidates from translating into effective CNS therapies (Pardridge 2005; Abbott et al. 2010). To bypass the BBB, invasive approaches such as intrathecal, intracerebroventricular, or convection-enhanced delivery are considered. However, their broader clinical use is constrained by procedural complexity, brain tissue injury, and the risk of infection (Lonser et al. 2015). To this end, nose-to-brain (N2B) delivery has emerged as a noninvasive approach with the potential to circumvent the BBB and offer broader clinical applicability and safer therapeutic access to the brain (Lochhead and Davis 2019; Wang et al. 2019; Keller et al. 2022).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Redefining intranasal brain delivery: from nasal entry to meaningful parenchymal and cellular exposure》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Multistage-aware design · s0004-s2001-p5】First, the design of the formulation can leverage hemodynamic drive and influx. Arterial pulsatility driven by cardiac cycles serves as the primary physical engine driving CSF into the perivascular channels (Iliff et al. 2013; Mestre et al. 2018). The dobutamine treatment, artificially amplifying arterial pulsatility, significantly accelerates paravascular CSF influx, whereas unilateral internal carotid artery ligation reduces pulsatility via drastically suppresses flow (Iliff et al. 2013). Secondly, modulating intra-tissue fluid exchange can be applied. For convective fluid to penetrate the dense brain parenchyma, efficient solute exchange between the CSF and ISF is mandatory (Iliff et al. 2012; Wang et al. 2025). Biologically, the expression and polarized localization of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) water channels at the astrocytic endfeet act as the molecular gatekeeper of this exchange (Iliff et al. 2012). Therefore, to maximize this fluid-to-tissue transfer, future co-delivery strategies could incorporate transient modulators of AQP4-dependent CSF-ISF exchange alongside the primary therapeutic cargo, or surface-functionalizing the nanocarrier itself with bio-responsive components designed to engage this perivascular exchange interface (Iliff et al. 2012; Simões et al. 2024). By temporally synchronizing the upregulation of this molecular gatekeeper with the arrival of the formulation in the CSF space, or by allowing the nanocarrier to actively breach the parenchymal gateway upon local contact with the astrocytic endfeet, these approaches enable highly precise, on-demand control over intra-tissue delivery kinetics. Lastly, to sustain continuous convective flow and prevent fluid stagnation, an unobstructed exit pathway is vital. CSF drainage is complexly wired not only to the arachnoid villi but also to perineural spaces, the cribriform plate route surrounding the olfactory nerve, and the nasal/dural lymphatic drainage networks (Proulx 2021; Spera et al. 2023). To address this, future formulations could be engineered to actively lower downstream hydrodynamic resistance. For example, nanocarriers designed for the sequential, spatiotemporal release of mild extracellular matrix-remodeling enzymes or lymphatic vasodilators (e.g. VEGF-C) at the exit sites could improve local obstruction, thereby regulating outflow pressure to ensure uninterrupted, deep-brain convective circulation (Song et al. 2020). Collectively, because CSF influx and glymphatic transport function as a dynamic circulation network responsive to physiological variables, N2B delivery platforms must look beyond static cargo characteristics such as size and charge. Instead, they must actively integrate patient hemodynamics (pulsatility), anatomical alignment (posture and AQP4 gatekeepers), and lymphatic clearance capacity into their core architecture (Iliff et al. 2012, 2013; Mestre et al. 2018; Proulx 2021).

【Disease-informed design · s0004-s2003-p2】The very first gate, the nasal mucosa, is profoundly altered by pathological states (Gizurarson 1993; Merkus et al. 1998; Min et al. 2015). In patients with chronic neurodegenerative diseases, systemic neuroinflammation or aging-associated comorbidities often impair MCC and drastically alter intranasal pH and mucus rheology (Gizurarson 1993; Merkus et al. 1998). Under chronic inflammatory conditions, epithelial tight junctions may already be compromised, and altered concentrations of inflammatory proteins in the disease-induced mucus can abnormally amplify non-specific binding with cationic nanocarriers (Cone 2009; Lai et al. 2009; Boegh and Nielsen 2015; Min et al. 2015). In such a pathological environment, mucoadhesive formulations designed for healthy mucosal surfaces may cause excessive aggregation, which ironically impedes epithelial transmigration.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Redefining intranasal brain delivery: from nasal entry to meaningful parenchymal and cellular exposure》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Stage-resolved experimental validation · s0004-s2004-p1】To date, many studies have relied on bulk, non-fractionated tissue readouts, such as whole-brain fluorescence imaging and total tissue homogenate assays, as proof of delivery success (Ahmad et al. 2017; Yokel 2020; Yokel 2022). Crucially, however, these compartment-blind metrics fail to reflect whether a vehicle is sequestered within intermediate boundary compartments, prematurely disrupted by pathological matrix forces, or rendered non-functional despite structural entry. Therefore, conventional readouts with a single quantitative value can create a general illusion of success that overestimates therapeutically relevant delivery. This methodological overestimation stems from three critical blind spots.

【Stage-resolved experimental validation · s0004-s2004-p2】First, bulk readouts can obscure sub-anatomical compartment localization. Even when a robust brain signal or imaging is observed, it cannot discern whether the formulation has penetrated the deep brain parenchyma or remains sequestered within intermediate boundary compartments. As shown by Lochhead et al., intranasal tracers exploit the PVS as a low-resistance convective highway for rapid, brain-wide redistribution (Lochhead et al. 2015). However, while this glymphatic-associated transit is a vital macro-transport pathway, a widespread perivascular signal must not be conflated with widespread parenchymal entry. Without high-resolution confocal or sheet-illumination microscopy to verify paracellular extravasation out of the PVS and into the deep interstitial space, bulk readouts can lead to a misinterpretation of a vehicle on the vascular periphery as a successfully delivered therapeutic.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Redefining intranasal brain delivery: from nasal entry to meaningful parenchymal and cellular exposure》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · f0001】Figure 1. Bottlenecks at the nasal deposition and retention stage. Four sequential barriers restrict therapeutic cargo from reaching the olfactory epithelium. 1) An aerodynamic bottleneck is imposed by the anterior nasal geometry. 2) A physical bottleneck arises from charge- and size-mediated drug entrapment within the mucus network. 3) A mucociliary bottleneck is driven by rapid mucociliary clearance (MCC). 4) A biochemical bottleneck results from local immunoglobulin A (IgA), hydrolytic enzymes, and low pH that promote early cargo degradation and inactivation. These compounded early-stage losses determine the functionally available fraction of the administered dose that can advance to epithelial crossing. Created with BioRender.com.

【Figure 2. · f0002】Figure 2. Overview of the three primary nasal epithelial crossing routes. The paracellular route and perineural bulk flow achieve central nervous system (CNS) exposure within seconds to minutes. Epithelial transcytosis operates on a timescale of 10 minutes to hours. Intraneuronal axonal transport requires hours to days. This timescale hierarchy determines which route governs the rapid initial CNS signal versus sustained cargo distribution. The mechanistic bottlenecks and cargo requirements for each route are summarized in Table 1. Created with BioRender.com.

【Figure 3. · f0003】Figure 3. Anatomical trajectories and stage-specific bottlenecks of the olfactory and trigeminal routes. Along the olfactory route, cargo migrates alongside olfactory nerve bundles through the cribriform plate toward the subarachnoid space (SAS) and olfactory bulb, encountering three principal bottlenecks: 1) a restricted physical bottleneck at the densely packed cribriform plate foramina and 2) a slow transport timescale for intraneuronal axonal transit. Along the trigeminal route, cargo migrates through perineuronal spaces of the trigeminal nerve (V) toward the brainstem and cerebellum via the SAS, encountering two bottlenecks: 1) a long transport axis from the nasal cavity to the posterior CNS, 2) fluidic resistance within the perineuronal space (PNS), and 3) a slow transport timescale for perineural transit. The olfactory route preferentially targets anterior CNS structures via cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-mediated redistribution, whereas the trigeminal route provides a conduit to the posterior and inferior CNS regions. Created with BioRender.com.
